definitions.explanation: To speak highly of someone (often to gain favor).

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる。
{上司|じょうし}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる。
みんなで{彼|かれ}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げている。
この{石|いし}は{重|おも}すぎて{一人|ひとり}では{持|も}ち{上|あ}げられない。
examples.english: This rock is too heavy to lift by myself.

examples.japanese: おだてて{持|も}ち{上|あ}げても、{彼|かれ}は{喜|よろこ}ばない。
examples.english: Even if you flatter him, he won't be pleased.

notes:
{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる is a compound verb meaning to lift up physically or to flatter.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle for the object

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{持|も}つ (to hold) + {上|あ}げる (to raise) = to lift up

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる: to lift luggage
- {箱|はこ}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる: to lift a box
- {人|ひと}を{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる: to flatter someone
- おだてて{持|も}ち{上|あ}げる: to butter someone up

FIGURATIVE USE:
The "flattery" meaning comes from the image of elevating someone with praise. Often used critically to describe insincere praise or sycophantic behavior.
